Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes

  • EKS Hybrid Nodes allow customers to use their own infrastructure as part of the EKS-managed cluster. These nodes become workers in the EKS cluster and can be physical or virtual with a limited number of operating system options. While AWS manages the control plane of the EKS cluster, the customer manages the on-premises nodes, thus unifying the Kubernetes management across the environment.

    • EKS Data Plane

    • Storage

Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes

  • EKS Control Plane

    The EKS Control Plane serves as the core management component of the EKS cluster. It contains all the pieces that make K8s work, managing the cluster’s state, API requests, and the scheduling of pods to the workers. The EKS Control Plane consists of the following components:

    • K8s API Server
    • etcd (key-value store)
    • Scheduler
    • Controller Manager
    • Cloud Controller Manager

Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes

  • EKS Data Plane

    The EKS Data Plane is the component that runs all the actual workloads consisting of applications, services, and data processing. It also controls networking and storing data. In an EKS Hybrid Nodes configuration the data plane is on-premises. The EKS Data Plane consists of the following components:

    • Worker nodes
    • Kubelet
    • Container runtime
    • Kube proxy
    • Applications/workloads

Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes

  • Networking

    To use the EKS Hybrid Nodes solution, it is critical to have a stable and fast network. Amazon EKS uses AWS networking components such as VPC, VPN, and Direct Connect to communicate securely between the AWS and on-premises resources.

  • Storage

Amazon EKS

  • Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) is a platform for running Kubernetes (K8s) clusters in both the Amazon Web Services (AWS) cloud and on-premises customer data centers. When a customer uses their own infrastructure as part of the solution, Amazon offers two options: EKS Anywhere or Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes. Amazon EKS simplifies the process of building, securing, and maintaining Kubernetes clusters. It uses one of two approaches: EKS standard or EKS Auto Mode. EKS Auto Mode is designed to manage both the control and data planes while EKS standard only manages the control plane.

Authentication and access control

  • Identity and Access Management, or IAM, is a service that lets you securely manage access to AWS services and resources. Essentially, IAM controls who is authenticated and what they are authorized to do in the AWS environment. The following requirements apply:

    • Hybrid Nodes IAM Role: Each node must assume a Hybrid Nodes IAM Role for authentication.
    • IAM Providers:
      • AWS IAM Roles Anywhere – Recommended for production.
      • AWS Systems Manager (SSM) Hybrid Activations – Simplifies testing and thus used in this solution.
    • API or API_AND_CONFIG_MAP mode must be used for Hybrid Nodes.
    • OIDC Authentication and IRSA: Supported for workloads that require IAM authentication.

AWS command parameters

  • Nodeadm install

    When running nodeadm install, the following files and file locations are configured.

    Table 4. Nodeadm install file locations
    Artifact Path
    IAM Roles Anywhere CLI /usr/local/bin/aws_signing_helper
    Kubelet binary /usr/bin/kubelet
    Kubectl binary usr/local/bin/kubectl
    ECR Credentials Provider /etc/eks/image-credential-provider/ecr-credential-provider
    AWS IAM Authenticator /usr/local/bin/aws-iam-authenticator
    SSM Setup CLI /opt/ssm/ssm-setup-cli
    SSM Agent

    Ubuntu: /snap/amazon-ssm-agent/current/amazon-ssm-agent

    RHEL and AL2023: /usr/bin/amazon-ssm-agent
    Containerd

    Ubuntu and AL2023: /usr/bin/containerd

    RHEL: /bin/containerd
    Iptables

    Ubuntu and AL2023: /usr/sbin/iptables

    RHEL: /sbin/iptables
    CNI plugins /opt/cni/bin
    installed artifacts tracker /opt/nodeadm/tracker

Home > Storage > PowerMax and VMAX > White Papers > Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes with Dell PowerMax > Configuring the EKS cluster

Configuring the EKS cluster

  • Additional configurations are required to ensure proper networking, authentication, and Kubernetes role-based access control (RBAC) after successfully deploying the AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes cluster. Perform these steps on the AWS jump box, which serves as the central administrative node for managing the hybrid Kubernetes environment.

    The kubectl CLI tool is required to manage Kubernetes resources on the EKS Hybrid Nodes cluster. It must be installed before proceeding with additional steps.

    1. Download kubectl

      Run the following command on the AWS jump box to download kubectl for the EKS Kubernetes version.

      curl -O https://s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/amazon-eks/1.32.0/2024-12-20/bin/linux/amd64/kubectl
    2. Modify the permissions of the binary and set the path.
      • chmod +x ./kubectl
      • mkdir -p $HOME/bin && cp ./kubectl $HOME/bin/kubectl && export PATH=$HOME/bin:$PATH
      • echo 'export PATH=$HOME/bin:$PATH' >> ~/.bashrc
    3. Update kubeconfig on the jump box
      • export REGION=”us-east-1”
      • export CLUSTER_NAME=”hybrid-eks”
      Verify the variables:
      • echo$REGION
      • echo $CLUSTER_NAME
      Command
      aws eks update-kubeconfig --region $REGION --name $CLUSTER_NAME
      Result
      Added new context arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:345087217345:cluster/hybrid-eks-cluster to \root\.kube\config
    4. Verify Installation.
      Command
      kubectl version
      Result
      Client Version: v1.32.0-eks-5ca49cb
Kustomize Version: v5.5.0
Server Version: v1.32.3-eks-bcf3d70

      The VPC CNI must be updated to avoid scheduling on Hybrid Nodes since it relies on AWS VPC networking resources which are not available for on-premises nodes. This is known as setting an anti-affinity rule. For this solution, it must be a hard rule, meaning AWS will never schedule the VPC CNI on the worker nodes.

    5. Create the update_scheduling.yaml file to modify scheduling of the VPC CNI.

      Create a file update_scheduling.yaml and add the following content.

      spec:
  template:
    spec:
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
            - matchExpressions:
              - key: kubernetes.io/os
                operator: In
                values:
                - linux
              - key: kubernetes.io/arch
                operator: In
                values:
                - amd64
                - arm64
              - key: eks.amazonaws.com/compute-type
                operator: NotIn
                values:
                - fargate
                - hybridStep
    6. Apply the patch to the VPC CNI.
      Command
      kubectl patch ds aws-node -n kube-system --type merge --patch-file=update_scheduling.yaml
      Result
      daemonset.apps/aws-node patched

      The IAM role must be mapped in the aws-auth ConfigMap to allow Hybrid Nodes to interact with the Kubernetes API and AWS resources.

    7. Retrieve IAM Role ARN.
      Command
      aws iam get-role --role-name AmazonEKSHybridNodesRole | grep Arn
      Result
      "Arn": "arn:aws:iam::345087217345:role/AmazonEKSHybridNodesRole",
        "ArnEquals": {
            "aws:SourceArn": "arn:aws:ssm:us-east-:345087217345:*"
    8. Check for an existing aws-auth ConfigMap.
      Command
      kubectl describe configmap -n kube-system aws-auth

      If the result returns the following, proceed to the next step; otherwise determine why this particular named config map exists as that is not the expectation.

      Result
      Error from server (NotFound): configmaps "aws-auth" not found
    9. Create the aws-auth ConfigMap.

      Create a file aws-auth-configmap.yaml and add the following content:

      apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: aws-auth
  namespace: kube-system
data:
  mapRoles: |
    - groups:
        - system:bootstrappers
        - system:nodes
      rolearn: "arn:aws:iam::345087217345:role/AmazonEKSHybridNodesRole"
      username: system:node:{{SessionName}}
    10. Apply the ConfigMap.
      Command
      kubectl apply -f aws-auth-configmap.yaml
      Result
      configmap/aws-auth created

Connect Hybrid Nodes

  • AWS relies on the binary nodeadm to initialize and configure the on-premises Hybrid Nodes. This binary is installed on each Hybrid Node. Follow the steps below to add the Hybrid Nodes to the EKS cluster.

    1. Download nodeadm.

      Run the following command on each Hybrid Node to retrieve the nodeadm from AWS.

      curl -OL
      'https://hybrid-assets.eks.amazonaws.com/releases/latest/bin/linux/amd64/nodeadm'
    2. Add executable permission. 
      chmod +x nodeadm
    3. Run the nodeadm install command.

      Run the following for the Kubernetes version 1.32 with the ssm credential provider. The nodeadm install command installs dependencies on the Hybrid Nodes including:

      • containerd
      • Kubelet
      • Kubectl
      • AWS SSM Agent
      • IAM Roles Anywhere components

      Run the following on each node.

      Command 
      ./nodeadm install 1.32 --credential-provider ssm
      Result 
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652448.883305,"caller":"install/install.go:96","msg":"Creating package manager..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652448.985312,"caller":"install/install.go:105","msg":"Validating Kubernetes version","kubernetes version":"1.32"}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652448.9883412,"caller":"install/install.go:111","msg":"Using Kubernetes version","kubernetes version":"1.32.1"}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652445.362858,"caller":"install/install.go:43","msg":"Configuring package manager. This might take a while..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652463.362879,"caller":"install/install.go:65","msg":"Installing containerd..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652461.1370873,"caller":"install/install.go:70","msg":"Installing iptables..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652461.137124,"caller":"install/install.go:84","msg":"Installing SSM agent installer..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652461.1373255,"caller":"fsm/source.go:113","msg":"Downloading SSM installer","region":"us-west-2","url":"https://amazon-ssm-us-west-2.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/latest/debian_amd64/ssm-setup-cli"}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652509.133477,"caller":"install/install.go:100","msg":"Installing kubelet..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652509.133497,"caller":"install/install.go:105","msg":"Installing kubectl..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652512.061429,"caller":"install/install.go:108","msg":"Installing cni-plugins..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652512.0614681,"caller":"install/install.go:115","msg":"Installing image credential provider..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652513.392943,"caller":"fsm/install.go:120","msg":"Installing IAM authenticator..."}
      {"level":"info","ts":1744652513.396267,"caller":"fsm/install.go:60","msg":"Finishing up install..."}

      Next, in order to connect each Hybrid Node to the EKS cluster, run nodeadm init. The command takes a config file as input that contains the cluster information and AWS Systems Manager (SSM) activation credentials previously recorded above.

    4. Create a config file.

      Create a configuration file (for example, nodeConfig.yaml) and populate it with the cluster details and SSM activation credentials. The same file is used on each Hybrid Node.

      Syntax: 

      apiVersion: node.eks.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: NodeConfig
      spec:
        cluster:
          name: <cluster-name>
          region: <aws-region>
        hybrid:
          ssm:
            activationCode: <ssm-activation-code>
            activationId: <ssm-activation-id>

      With supplied parameters:

      apiVersion: node.eks.aws/v1alpha1
      kind: NodeConfig
      spec:
        cluster: 
          name: hybrid-eks
          region: us-east-1
        hybrid:
          ssm:
            activationCode: "ESQx1lwstRT6TqOEH9dZ"
            activationId: "c355490f-2c7f-987b-8068-c364e3fddc7b"
    5. Run the node initialization command.

      Supply the configuration file to the nodeadm init command. Run this same command, with the same config file on each Hybrid Node.

      ./nodeadm init -c file://nodeConfig.yaml

      This command adds the Hybrid Node as a worker to the cluster.

    6. Verify worker nodes.

      To confirm that the workers successfully joined the cluster, run the following command:

      Command 
      kubectl get nodes
      Result 
      NAME                            STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
      mi-0d44c195f4b45b1c2            NotReady   <none>   18h   v1.32.1-eks-5d632ec
      mi-0f3cddec9de55bf61            NotReady   <none>   18h   v1.32.1-eks-5d632ec
      mi-0f64ac7b460195948            NotReady   <none>   18h   v1.32.1-eks-5d632ec

      Newly added nodes have a status of NotReady because the CNI is not yet deployed on Hybrid Nodes. Note also that the worker nodes are assigned names, they do not use their hostnames.

    7. Check the AWS UI for the worker nodes.

      If desired, you can view the worker nodes in the AWS UI. Log in to your account and navigate to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service > Clusters > <cluster_name> > Compute. Note the Compute column shows Hybrid and the Status as Not ready. An example for this cluster is shown in the following figure.

Create EKS cluster

  • This section outlines the steps required to deploy an AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes cluster using the CloudFormation template method. Run the following steps on the AWS jump box.

    The CloudFormation template automates the creation of essential resources for the EKS Hybrid Nodes cluster, including:

    • EKS cluster security group
    • EKS cluster IAM role
    • EKS cluster
    1. Download the CloudFormation template.

      Run the following command on the AWS jump box to download the EKS Hybrid Nodes CloudFormation template:

      curl -OL 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aws/eks-hybrid/refs/heads/main/example/hybrid-eks-cfn.yaml'

      A JSON configuration file is required to specify networking details such as cluster name, subnets, and remote CIDR ranges for communication between AWS and on-premises resources. See the AWS user guide in AWS documentation for explanations of all the parameters if desired.

    2. Create a cfn-eks-parameters.json file.
      {
  "Parameters": {
    "ClusterName": "CLUSTER_NAME",
    "ClusterRoleName": "CLUSTER_ROLE_NAME",
    "SubnetId1": "SUBNET1_ID",
    "SubnetId2": "SUBNET2_ID",
    "SecurityGroupId": "SG_ID",
    "RemoteNodeCIDR": "REMOTE_NODE_CIDRS",
    "RemotePodCIDR": "REMOTE_POD_CIDRS",
    "ClusterAuthMode": "CLUSTER_AUTH",
    "ClusterEndpointConnectivity": "CLUSTER_ENDPOINT",
    "K8sVersion": "K8S_VERSION"
  }
}

      Replace the parameters as appropriate for your environment.

      {
  "Parameters": {
    "ClusterName": "hybrid-eks",
    "ClusterRoleName": "ClusterRoleEKS",
    "SubnetId1": "subnet-06f77d28ev8884732",
    "SubnetId2": "subnet-0e1f0be2ae8884732",
    "SecurityGroupId" "sg-0825cc62f8873925e",
    "RemoteNodeCIDR": "10.228.xxx.xxx/29",
    "RemotePodCIDR": "10.44.xxx.xxx/23",
    "ClusterAuthMode": "API_AND_CONFIG_MAP",
    "ClusterEndpointConnectivity": "Private",
    "K8sVersion": "1.32"
  }
 }

      Once the CloudFormation template and parameter files are ready, deploy the cluster.

    3. Deploy CloudFormation stack.

      Run the following command on the AWS jump box to initiate deployment:

      Command
      export STACK_NAME=hybrid-ssm-cluster
aws cloudformation deploy \
 --stack-name ${STACK_NAME} \
 --template-file hybrid-eks-cfn.yaml \
 --parameter-overrides file://cfn-eks-parameters.json \
 --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM
      Result
      Waiting for changeset to be created..
Waiting for stack create/update to complete
Successfully created/updated stack - hybrid-ssm-cluster
    4. Describe the EKS Cluster.

      After the deployment is complete, verify that the EKS Hybrid Nodes cluster is active and properly configured.

      Command
      aws eks describe-cluster --name hybrid-eks --endpoint-url https://eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
      Result
      "cluster": {
        "name": "hybrid-eks",
        "arn": "arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:345087217345:cluster/hybrid-eks",
        "createdAt": "2025-04-09T17:21:17.902000+00:00",
        "version": "1.32",
        "endpoint": "https://22136AF8C4C8052958318F05AD2375D2.gr7.us-east-1.eks.amazonaws.com",
        "roleArn": "arn:aws:iam::345087217345:role/ClusterRoleEKS",
        "resourcesVpcConfig": {
            "subnetIds": [
                "subnet-06f77d28ev8884732",
                "subnet-0e1f0be2ae8884732"
            ],
            "securityGroupIds": [
                "sg-0825cc62f8873925e "
            ],
            "clusterSecurityGroupId": "sg-0825cc62f8873925e",
            "vpcId": "vpc-06cd86a0473348929",
            "endpointPublicAccess": false,
            "endpointPrivateAccess": true,
            "publicAccessCidrs": []
        },
        "kubernetesNetworkConfig": {
            "serviceIpv4Cidr": "172.16.0.0/16",
            "ipFamily": "ipv4",
            "elasticLoadBalancing": {
                "enabled": false
            }
        },
        },
        "logging": {
            "clusterLogging": [
                {
                    "types": [
                        "api",
                        "audit",
                        "authenticator",
                        "controllerManager",

                    ],
                    "enabled": false
                }
            ]
        },
        "identity": {
            "oidc": {
                "issuer": "https://oidc.eks.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/id/22136AF8C4C8052958318F05AD2375D2"
            }
        },
        "status": "ACTIVE",

      The "status": "ACTIVE" field confirms that the cluster has been successfully deployed. If desired, you can view the cluster status in the AWS UI. Log in to your account and navigate to Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service > Clusters > <cluster_name> as shown in the following figure.

CSI driver for Dell PowerMax on AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes

  • CSI installation

    In order to provision persistent storage from the PowerMax, install the Dell PowerMax CSI driver. The installation of the CSI driver requires a Linux EC2 jump box instance such as Amazon Linux 2023. It can be the same jump box used for the EKS cluster creation, however Windows, even with an emulation like Git Bash, is not supported. Once you supply the AWS credentials, run kubectl get nodes to ensure you are connected to your cluster.

    Note: The implementation of the PowerMax CSI driver on EKS Hybrid Nodes requires important changes to cert manager without which the pods will not run. These instructions are included in Step 3 and must be followed closely.

    Command 
    kubectl get nodes
    Result 
    NAME                   STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
    mi-0d44c195f4b45b1c2   Ready    <none>   10d   v1.32.1-eks-5d632ec
    mi-0f3cddec9de55bf61   Ready    <none>   10d   v1.32.1-eks-5d632ec
    mi-0f64ac7b460195948   Ready    <none>   10d   v1.32.1-eks-5d632ec
    Note: When using an EKS Hybrid Nodes cluster, you cannot manage the Kubernetes cluster from any of the Hybrid Nodes. Creation of workloads (pods) is performed from the jump box and includes the PowerMax CSI driver.

    The following steps walk through a helm-based installation of the driver. Be sure the jump host has helm installed. Although these steps should result in a successful installation, please refer to the latest documentation for new releases at: https://dell.github.io/csm-docs/docs/deployment/helm/drivers/installation/powermax/.

Home > Storage > PowerMax and VMAX > White Papers > Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes with Dell PowerMax > CSI driver for Dell PowerMax on AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes

CSI driver for Dell PowerMax on AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes

  • Prerequisites

    Some prerequisite steps are not included in these instructions as they vary across environments. For instance, each protocol (for example, iSCSI, NFS) has specific requirements in the documentation. In this solution, the Hybrid Nodes are attached to the PowerMax array through Fibre Channel (FC) and therefore those prerequisites were followed. Also this solution uses volume snapshots but it is an optional component of the CSI driver.

    1. Clone the Dell PowerMax CSI repository

      To begin, clone the PowerMax CSI GitHub repository on the AWS jump box:

      git clone -b v2.13.0 https://github.com/dell/csi-powermax.git
    2. Create a namespace for the PowerMax CSI driver.

      The CSI driver requires a namespace. The default in all the scripts is powermax so that is preferable.

      kubectl create namespace powermax
    3. CSI PowerMax Reverse Proxy

      The CSI PowerMax reverse proxy is an HTTPS server and has to be configured with an SSL certificate and a private key. As part of the proxy, you must install cert-manager which manages certificates and secrets. Unfortunately the use of cert-manager in the default configuration causes an issue with EKS Hybrid Nodes because of Calico CNI and webhook.

      You must make two changes to the cert-manager.yaml file before applying it.

      1. Download the cert-manager.yaml.

        First, download the file.

        curl -LO
https://github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/releases/download/v1.11.0/cert-manager.yaml
      2. Modify the cert-manager.yaml.

        Open the file and modify the following values under the cert-manager-webhook deployment.

        apiVersion: apps/v1 
kind: Deployment 
metadata: 
  name: cert-manager-webhook
  …

        Make the following port changes and add two new values to the deployment. The port value should be any number higher than 10250 (same number for both) and the two parameters in the spec section are new:

        args:
          - --v=2
          - --secure-port=10250 change to 10260
          …
  ports:
          - name: https
            protocol: TCP
            containerPort: 10250 change to 10260
            …
spec:
      hostNetwork: true <- Add here   
      dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet <- Add here
      serviceAccountName: cert-manager-webhook
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
          …

        After you make the changes, save the file and apply the cert-manager.yaml with kubectl. Part of the output is included below.

        Command
        kubectl apply -f cert-manager.yaml
        Output (partial)
        namespace/cert-manager created
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/clusterissuers.cert-manager.io created
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/challenges.acme.cert-manager.io created
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/certificaterequests.cert-manager.io created
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/issuers.cert-manager.io created
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/certificates.cert-manager.io created
…

        Check that the containers are running in the namespace.

        Command
        kubectl get pods -n cert-manager
        Result
        NAME                                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
cert-manager-7659df9f47-kx4wj              1/1     Running   0          63m
cert-manager-cainjector-5b8f8c75b9-5z2q9   1/1     Running   0          63m
cert-manager-webhook-5675fc4f47-gt2mq      1/1     Running   0          63m
    4. Create a secret for the Reverse Proxy.

      The following example shows how to generate a private key and then use that key to sign an SSL certificate using the openssl tool. The generated .key and .crt file is used to create a secret.

      1. Create the openssl.cnf file.

        Start by creating a configuration file called openssl.cnf with the following information. If desired, you can change the information under the [ req_distinguised_name ] section.

        [ req ]
default_bits       = 2048
distinguished_name = req_distinguished_name
req_extensions     = req_ext
prompt             = no

[ req_distinguished_name ]
C  = XX
L  = Default City
O  = Default Company Ltd

[ req_ext ]
subjectAltName = @alt_names

[ alt_names ]
DNS.1 = "csipowermax-reverseproxy"
IP.1 = "0.0.0.0"
      2. Create the secret.

        Now run the following to create the secret.

        Commands
        openssl genrsa -out tls.key 2048

openssl req -new -key tls.key -out tls.csr -config openssl.cnf

openssl x509 -req -in tls.csr -signkey tls.key -out tls.crt -days 3650 -extensions req_ext -extfile openssl.cnf

kubectl create secret -n powermax tls csirevproxy-tls-secret --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key
        Result
        Certificate request self-signature ok
subject=C=XX, L=Default City, O=Default Company Ltd
secret/csirevproxy-tls-secret created
    5. Create a secret for Unisphere for PowerMax credentials.

      Locate the secret.yaml file in the downloaded repository.

      /…/csi-powermax/samples/secret/secret.yaml

      Modify the username and password by supplying the base64 of those values. An example using the default Unisphere credentials is below as this is a test environment. Normally the user and password would be different.

      echo -n smc | base64
echo -n smc | base64

      The syntax for the secret is below with the values bolded for the username and password:

      apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: powermax-creds
  namespace: powermax
type: Opaque
data:
  # set username to the base64 encoded username
  # if authorization is enabled, username will be ignored
  username: c21j < base64 of smc
  # set password to the base64 encoded password
  # if authorization is enabled, password will be ignored
  password: c21j < base64 of smc
  # Uncomment the following key if you wish to use ISCSI CHAP authentication (v1.3.0 onwards)
  # chapsecret: <base64 CHAP secret>
      Command
      kubectl create -f secret.yaml
      Result
      secret/powermax-creds created
    6. Download the default values.yaml.

      The values file tells the installer what components to configure.

      cd /…/csi-powermax/dell-csi-helm-installer
      wget -O my-powermax-settings.yaml https://github.com/dell/helm-charts/raw/csi-powermax-2.13.0/charts/csi-powermax/values.yaml

      Modify my-powermax-settings.yaml to include, at a minimum:

      • Transport protocol
      • Unisphere for PowerMax endpoints
      • PowerMax arrays

      Example snippet:

      transportProtocol: "FC"
  storageArrays:
    - storageArrayId: "000120001111"
      endpoint: https://10.228.xxx.xxx:8443
      backupEndpoint: https://10.228.xxx.xxx:8443
  # - storageArrayId: "000000000002"
  #   endpoint: https://primary-2.unisphe.re:8443
  #   backupEndpoint: https://backup-2.unisphe.re:8443
  managementServers:
    - endpoint: https://10.228.xxx.xxx:8443
      credentialsSecret: powermax-creds
      skipCertificateValidation: true
      certSecret: csirevproxy-tls-secret
      limits:
        maxActiveRead: 5
        maxActiveWrite: 4
        maxOutStandingRead: 50
        maxOutStandingWrite: 50
    - endpoint: https://10.228.xxx.xxx:8443
      credentialsSecret: powermax-creds
      skipCertificateValidation: true

      To see all the possible values, see PowerMax CSI driver values file parameters.

    7. Modify helm chart.

      Because EKS Hybrid Nodes use a modified name for the Kubernetes server version, you must modify the Chart.yaml file to prevent the installer from erroring. First determine the Server Version by running the following command.

      Command
      kubectl version|grep Server
      Result
      Server Version: v1.32.3-eks-bcf3d70

      Next, open the file /…/csi-powermax/helm-charts/charts/csi-powermax/Chart.yaml and comment-out the current kubeVersion and replace it with your version from above. Save the file.

      apiVersion: v2
appVersion: "2.13.0"
name: csi-powermax
version: 2.13.0
description: |
  PowerMax CSI (Container Storage Interface) driver Kubernetes
  integration. This chart includes everything required to provision via CSI as
  well as a PowerMax StorageClass.
type: application
kubeVersion: ">= v1.32.3-eks-bcf3d70" < add
# If you are using a complex K8s version like "v1.23.3-mirantis-1", use this kubeVersion check instead
# kubeVersion: ">= 1.23.0-0" < comment out
    8. Install the PowerMax CSI Driver using helm.

      Run the following command to install the PowerMax CSI driver.

      ./csi-install.sh --namespace powermax --values my-powermax-settings.yaml

      The script runs through several pre-checks, some of which may fail expectedly. For example, the script tests for iSCSI even if you are not using that protocol. It will also look for snapshot and replication CRDs, optional components. These failures are in red in the following figure.

      After accepting the warnings, the script will indicate it is installing the driver. Because of the changes required for EKS and cert-manager, the script will report an internal error after some time at this prompt: |- Installing Driver. It does this at the end of the script, after completing all tasks. Though it says that the installation cannot continue, it is actually complete. It is not possible to avoid the error, so checking the statuses of the pods is the only way to see if the script was successful. All detail of the installation is shown in the following figure.

      A check of the CSI driver pods (included in the image but enlarged below) shows everything is running correctly with some common RESTARTS reported.

      Command
      kubectl get pods -n powermax
      Result
      NAME                                   READY   STATUS    RESTARTS        AGE
powermax-controller-79764db47b-dzzkp   6/6     Running   8 (3m46s ago)   3m56s
powermax-controller-79764db47b-phrcx   6/6     Running   8 (3m46s ago)   3m56s
powermax-node-4cgwf                    2/2     Running   2 (3m25s ago)   3m56s
powermax-node-9498c                    2/2     Running   1 (3m25s ago)   3m56s
powermax-node-nv8xf                    2/2     Running   2 (3m25s ago)   3m56s

Home > Storage > PowerMax and VMAX > White Papers > Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes with Dell PowerMax > CSI driver for Dell PowerMax on AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes

CSI driver for Dell PowerMax on AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes

  • Configure storage and snapshot volume classes

    When the driver installation completes, create storage and snapshot volume (if desired) classes. Storage classes are necessary in order to create persistent volumes. A storage class defines the characteristics of a volume. In the case of the PowerMax, this can include service level, expandability, host I/O limits, and file system type. Samples can be found in /…/csi-powermax/samples/storageclass.

    The following creates a diamond service level storage class which allows expansion and has a file system type of xfs. This storage class is configured so that when you create a PV, the device will not be created on the array until a request is made for it (WaitForFirstConsumer).

    1. Diamond storage class

      Create powermax-xfs-diamond.yaml with the following details.

      apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: powermax-xfs-diamond
parameters:
  csi.storage.k8s.io/fstype: xfs
  SRP: "SRP_1"
  SYMID: "000120001111"
  ServiceLevel: "Diamond"
provisioner: csi-powermax.dellemc.com
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
allowVolumeExpansion: true
      Command
      kubectl create -f powermax-xfs-diamond.yaml
      Result
      storageclass.storage.k8s.io/powermax-diamond-xfs created

      You can create as many storage classes as you must meet the requirements of the applications. In addition to the diamond class, a bronze class was added for purposes of the application test in Application deployments.

    2. VolumeSnapshotClass

      As the next chapter will be demonstrating snapshots, create a volume snapshot class for the PowerMax. The sample script v1_powermax-snapclass.yaml in /…/csi-powermax/samples/volumesnapshotclass is sufficient for this purpose.

      apiVersion: snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: VolumeSnapshotClass
metadata:
  name: powermax-snapclass
driver: csi-powermax.dellemc.com
deletionPolicy: Delete
      Command
      kubectl create -f v1_powermax-snapclass.yaml
      Result
      volumesnapshotclass.snapshot.storage.k8s.io/powermax-snapclass created
    3. Verification

      To verify the storage classes, run the following. Note that during the EKC cluster creation, AWS automatically creates a storage class for gp2 storage.

      Command
      kubectl get sc
      Result
      NAME                   PROVISIONER                RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE      ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION   AGE
gp2                    kubernetes.io/aws-ebs      Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer   false                  16d
powermax-xfs-bronze    csi-powermax.dellemc.com   Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer   true                   8s
powermax-xfs-diamond   csi-powermax.dellemc.com   Delete          WaitForFirstConsumer   true                   15s

      To verify the volume snapshot class, run the following.

      Command
      kubectl get vsclass
      Result
      NAME                 DRIVER                     DELETIONPOLICY   AGE
powermax-snapclass   csi-powermax.dellemc.com   Delete           11d

Dell PowerMax storage

  • Dell PowerMax integrates with Kubernetes through the Dell PowerMax Container Storage Interface or CSI driver. The CSI driver enables the dynamic provisioning of persistent volumes (PVs) from the PowerMax for applications in the EKS cluster. Each PV is associated with a storage class which defines the characteristics of the volume such as what service level (SLA) it should be assigned, whether it can be expanded, what file system format it should get, and so forth. A user can create multiple storage classes to ensure that when a PV is bound to a containerized application, it embodies the correct characteristics.

    Additionally, Dell offers Container Storage Modules (CSM), which are used alongside the CSI driver. PowerMax supports CSM capabilities for authorization, observability, replication, resiliency, snapshots, and application mobility.

Executive summary

  • Companies are increasingly looking at hybrid cloud architectures to balance scalability, performance, and security requirements. Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) Hybrid Nodes allow enterprises to deploy Kubernetes clusters that run both on AWS and on-premises infrastructure. Integrating Dell PowerMax—a leading enterprise storage array known for its ultra-low latency, extreme scalability, and robust data services—further enhances this architecture by delivering powerful external storage capabilities to Kubernetes workloads.

    By deploying EKS Hybrid Nodes that connect to Dell PowerMax storage arrays:

    • Enterprises can extend EKS into their own data centers while maintaining a consistent operational model across cloud and on-premises environments.
    • Dell PowerMax provides high-performance block storage to Kubernetes applications through Container Storage Interface (CSI) drivers, enabling persistent volumes for critical stateful workloads. PowerMax offers features like snapshotting, replication, and encryption, enhancing resilience and compliance for mission-critical applications.
    • The Hybrid Nodes solution supports use cases like data locality, regulatory compliance, disaster recovery, and scalability.

    The combination of Amazon EKS and Dell PowerMax ensures that businesses can modernize with Kubernetes while optimizing infrastructure investments, maintaining data control, and achieving cloud-native agility.

    Note: The contents of this document are valid for the software and hardware versions described. Always refer to the latest PowerMax and Amazon documentation before beginning an implementation.

Install CNI

  • You must install a Container Network Interface (CNI) on the Hybrid Nodes for them to be fully operational and serve workloads. Dell Technologies recommends using Calico as it provides networking and security features for Kubernetes environments.

    1. Add the Calico helm repository.

      Run the following command on the jump box to add the Calico helm repository.

      Command 
      helm repo add projectcalico https://docs.tigera.io/calico/charts
      Result 
      "projectcalico" has been added to your repositories

      Calico must be configured to assign IPs to pods running on Hybrid Nodes. This is done by creating a custom values file (calico-values.yaml).

    2. Create the calico-values.yaml file.

      Create a file named calico-values.yaml and define the CNI type, Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) setting, and Pod CIDR. The CNI type is Calico, BGP should be enabled, and the Pod CIDR should match the RemotePodCIDR parameter specified in the Create EKS cluster section.

      Syntax:

      installation:
        cni:
          type: Calico
          calicoNetwork:
            bgp: Enabled
            ipPools:
              - cidr: <PodCIDR>

      With supplied parameters:

      installation:
        cni:
          type: Calico
          calicoNetwork:
            bgp: Enabled
            ipPools:
              - cidr: "10.44.x.x/23"
    3. Create the tigera-operator namespace.
      Command 
      kubectl create namespace tigera-operator
      Result 
      namespace/tigera-operator created
    4. Install Calico using helm.
      Command 
      helm install calico projectcalico/tigera-operator --version v3.29.3 -f calico-values.yaml --namespace tigera-operator
      Result 
      NAME: calico
      LAST DEPLOYED: Tue Apr 15 13:13:17 2025
      NAMESPACE: tigera-operator
      STATUS: deployed
      REVISION: 1
      TEST SUITE: None

      After installing Calico, check that the containers are running and that the Hybrid Nodes have a status of Ready. If the Calico containers are not in a Running status, check the pod log files for networking errors.

      Command 
      kubectl get pods -n calico-system
      Result 
      NAME                                            READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
      calico-kube-controllers-76f946b87c-nrldt        1/1     Running   0          16m
      calico-node-2h1x4                               1/1     Running   0          15m
      calico-node-m8ffq                               1/1     Running   0          15m
      calico-node-rndcf                               1/1     Running   0          15m
      calico-typha-7879b4d599-pbvgb                   1/1     Running   0          16m
      calico-typha-7879b4d599-th4nd                   1/1     Running   0          16m
      csi-node-driver-95jwq                           2/2     Running   0          16m
      csi-node-driver-dzv54                           2/2     Running   0          16m
      csi-node-driver-lhsrs                           2/2     Running   0          16m
      Command 
      kubectl get nodes
      Result 
      NAME                   STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
      mi-0d44c195f4b45b1c2   Ready    <none>   18h   v1.32.1-eks-5d632ec
      mi-0f3cddec9de55bf61   Ready    <none>   18h   v1.32.1-eks-5d632ec
      mi-0f64ac7b460195948   Ready    <none>   18h   v1.32.1-eks-5d632ec

      This completes the EKS Hybrid Nodes implementation. The next chapter will cover implementing the CSI driver for Dell PowerMax which enables persistent storage for stateful application workloads.

MySQL deployment

  • This section outlines a deployment of MySQL on Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes using Dell PowerMax as persistent storage.

    1. Create a namespace for the MySQL deployment.
      Command
      kubectl create namespace mysql
      Result
      namespace/mysql created
    2. Create a PVC for MySQL in the diamond storage class.

      Recall that the storage class is set to wait for the pod to deploy and therefore this will not generate a device. The diamond storage class indicates that this implementation is for production.

      apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: mysql-pvc
spec:
  storageClassName: powermax-xfs-diamond
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 70G
      Command
      kubectl create -f mysql-pvc.yaml -n mysql
      Result
      persistentvolumeclaim/mysql-pvc created

      Now check for the PVC. Note here the STATUS is Pending and thus there is no device created yet.

      Command
      kubectl get pvc -n mysql
      Result
      NAME        STATUS    VOLUME   CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS          VOLUMEATTRIBUTESCLASS   AGE
mysql-pvc   Pending                                      powermax-xfs-diamond   <unset>                 6m39s
    3. Deploy MySQL.

      In this step, deploy the MySQL pod. The pod is configured with the previous PVC which therefore will initiate the device creation and presentation of it in a masking view to the worker node.

      apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: mysql-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: mysql
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: mysql
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: mysql
        image: mysql:8.0
        env:
        - name: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD
          value: "xxxxxxxx”
        - name: MYSQL_DATABASE
          value: "mysqldb"
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3306
        volumeMounts:
        - name: mysql-storage
          mountPath: /var/lib/mysql
      volumes:
      - name: mysql-storage
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: mysql-pvc
      Command
      kubectl create -f mysql.yaml -n mysql
      Result
      deployment.apps/mysql-deployment created

      And now the PV and PVC are present. Note the STATUS column indicates Bound.

      Command
      kubectl get pv
      Result
      NAME                CAPACITY     ACCESS MODES   RECLAIM POLICY   STATUS   CLAIM               STORAGECLASS          VOLUMEATTRIBUTESCLASS   REASON   AGE
csivol-52dd6ecdf4   68359680Ki   RWO            Delete           Bound    mysql/mysql-pvc   powermax-xfs-diamond  <unset>                          3m28s
      Command
      kubectl get pvc
      Result
      NAME        STATUS   VOLUME              CAPACITY     ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS          VOLUMEATTRIBUTESCLASS   AGE
mysql-pvc   Bound    csivol-52dd6ecdf4   68359680Ki   RWO            powermax-xfs-diamond   <unset>                 12mf
    4. Create a MySQL service.

      To access MySQL from a MySQL client on a host, create a service to allow port access.

      apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: mysql-service
  namespace: mysql
spec:
  selector:
    app: mysql
  ports:
    - port: 3306       # MySQL default port
      targetPort: 3306  # MySQL container port
      protocol: TCP
      nodePort: 32000   # Choose a port in the range 30000-32767
  type: NodePort
      Command
      kubectl create -f mysql-service.yaml -n mysql
      Result
      service/mysql-service created

      View the service. The node port, 32000, is the one used to attach to MySQL.

      Command
      kubectl get service -n mysql
      Result
      NAME            TYPE       CLUSTER-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   PORT(S)          AGE
mysql-service   NodePort   172.16.252.72   <none>        3306:32000/TCP   24sb
    5. Access MySQL

      To access MySQL you must first know the worker node and IP where the pod is running. From this command below you can get the node name and then by running the second command you can see the node has an IP of 10.228.xxx.xx2. They are bolded below for easier recognition. Although the node port is accessible on the first IP (172.16.x.x), you could only run the MySQL client from a worker node which is not recommended. Using the 10.228.x.x network means any system on the corporate subnet can be used.

      Command
      kubectl get pod -n mysql -o wide
      Result
      NAME                               READY   STATUS   IP              NODE                   
mysql-deployment-bfbc59fb8-hw5nw   1/1     Running  172.16.151.81   mi-0f3cddec9de55bf61
      Command
      kubectl get nodes -o wide
      Result
      NAME                   STATUS   INTERNAL-IP      EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE             
mi-0d44c195f4b45b1c2   Ready    10.228.xxx.xx1   <none>        Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS   
mi-0f3cddec9de55bf61   Ready    10.228.xxx.xx2   <none>        Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS   
mi-0f64ac7b460195948   Ready    10.228.xxx.xx3   <none>        Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS

      Log in to a system on the same corporate network as the Hybrid Nodes and attach to the MySQL database running in the EKS cluster through the previously configured node port.

      Command
      mysql -h 10.228.xxx.xx2  -P32000 -uroot -p
Enter password:
      Result
      Welcome to the MySQL monitor.  Commands end with ; or \g.
Your MySQL connection id is 12
Server version: 8.0.42 MySQL Community Server - GPL

Copyright (c) 2000, 2025, Oracle and/or its affiliates.

Oracle is a registered trademark of Oracle Corporation and/or its
affiliates. Other names may be trademarks of their respective
owners.

Type 'help;' or '\h' for help. Type '\c' to clear the current input statement.

mysql> show databases;
+--------------------+
| Database           |
+--------------------+
| information_schema |
| mysql              |
| mysqldb            |
| performance_schema |
| sys                |
+--------------------+
5 rows in set (0.00 sec)

mysql>

MySQL deployment

  • Snapshots and clones

    For the second part of the application test, create a test database by taking a snapshot of the MySQL volume and then creating a clone from it. That clone will be the basis for a second MySQL deployment, or test setup. The following figure is a simple rendering of the workflow for this test.


    MySQL sample_db

    To distinguish the clone from a default MySQL implementation, create a sample database in the production MySQL. This example uses a three-table database named sample_db. Each table is filled with ten rows.

    1. Create sample_db.
      -- Create the database
CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS sample_db;
USE sample_db;

-- Create the 'users' table
CREATE TABLE users (
    user_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    username VARCHAR(50),
    email VARCHAR(100),
    created_at DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

-- Create the 'products' table
CREATE TABLE products (
    product_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    product_name VARCHAR(100),
    price DECIMAL(10,2),
    stock INT
);

-- Create the 'orders' table
CREATE TABLE orders (
    order_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id INT,
    product_id INT,
    quantity INT,
    order_date DATETIME DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(user_id),
    FOREIGN KEY (product_id) REFERENCES products(product_id)
);
    2. Insert data into sample_db
      -- Insert sample data into 'users'
INSERT INTO users (username, email) VALUES
('alice', 'alice@example.com'),
('bob', 'bob@example.com'),
('charlie', 'charlie@example.com'),
('dave', 'dave@example.com'),
('eve', 'eve@example.com'),
('frank', 'frank@example.com'),
('grace', 'grace@example.com'),
('heidi', 'heidi@example.com'),
('ivan', 'ivan@example.com'),
('judy', 'judy@example.com');

-- Insert sample data into 'products'
INSERT INTO products (product_name, price, stock) VALUES
('Laptop', 999.99, 50),
('Smartphone', 699.99, 100),
('Tablet', 399.99, 75),
('Monitor', 199.99, 30),
('Keyboard', 49.99, 200),
('Mouse', 29.99, 150),
('Printer', 149.99, 40),
('Camera', 499.99, 25),
('Speaker', 89.99, 80),
('Router', 59.99, 60);

-- Insert sample data into 'orders'
INSERT INTO orders (user_id, product_id, quantity) VALUES
(1, 2, 1),
(2, 1, 2),
(3, 5, 3),
(4, 4, 1),
(5, 3, 2),
(6, 6, 1),

    Snapshot

    Take a snapshot of the MySQL PVC which now incorporates the new database. Create a file called mysql_snapshot.yaml for this purpose.

    apiVersion: snapshot.storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: VolumeSnapshot
metadata:
  name: mysql-snapshot
  namespace: mysql
spec:
  volumeSnapshotClassName: powermax-snapclass
  source:
    persistentVolumeClaimName: mysql-pvc
    Command
    kubectl create -f mysql_snapshot.yaml -n mysql
    Result
    volumesnapshot.snapshot.storage.k8s.io/mysql-snapshot created

    The newly created snapshot is seen here in the following figure in Unisphere for PowerMax.


    Clone to PVC

    Now clone the snapshot to a new PVC for the test environment. Create a file called mysql_clone.yaml to do this. Since this is a test environment, change the storage class to bronze from diamond.

    apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: cloned-mysql-pvc
  namespace: mysql
spec:
  storageClassName: powermax-xfs-bronze
  dataSource:
    name: mysql-snapshot
    kind: VolumeSnapshot
    apiGroup: snapshot.storage.k8s.io
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 70Gi

    Create the PVC. As before, the STATUS is Pending because the storage class dictates to wait for the first consumer which in this case will be the MySQL test pod.

    Command
    kubectl create -f mysql_clone.yaml
    Result
    persistentvolumeclaim/cloned-mysql-pvc created

    Command:

    Result:

    Query the PVC.

    Command
    kubectl get pvc -n mysql
    Result

cloned-mysql-pvc   Pending                                                   powermax-xfs-bronze   <unset>                 19s
mysql-pvc          Bound     csivol-12cc4e6b82   68359680Ki   RWO            powermax-xfs-diamond   <unset>                 2d23h

    Next, create the test MySQL deployment.

    MySQL test deployment

    1. Deploy test MySQL.

      Create a file mysql_test.yaml which uses the cloned-mysql-pvc claim.

      apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: mysql-deployment-test
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: mysql-test
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: mysql-test
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: mysql-test
        image: mysql:8.0
        env:
        - name: MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD
          value: "xxxxxxxxx"
        - name: MYSQL_DATABASE
          value: "mysqldb"
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3306
        volumeMounts:
        - name: mysql-storage-test
          mountPath: /var/lib/mysql
      volumes:
      - name: mysql-storage-test
        persistentVolumeClaim:
          claimName: cloned-mysql-pvc
      Command
      kubectl create -f mysql_test.yaml -n mysql
      Result
      deployment.apps/mysql-deployment-test created

kind: Service
metadata:

spec:

Networking

  • Speed and connectivity

    AWS recommends a minimum of 100 Mbps in between the Hybrid Nodes and AWS and a maximum of 200 ms round trip latency. The communication between the Amazon EKS Control Plane and Hybrid Nodes is routed through the VPC and subnets that you pass during cluster creation. This builds on the existing mechanism in Amazon EKS for control plane to node networking. There are several documented options available for you to connect your on-premises environment with your VPC including AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, or your own VPN connection.

    Cluster API Access requires public or private API endpoints for Hybrid Nodes using IPv4. IPv6 is not supported. Do not use the public and private option as DNS will cause issues. Similarly, your on-premises node and Pod CIDRs must be IPv4 RFC1918 CIDR blocks.

Networking

  • Routing and firewalls

    The following applies to routing:

    • VPC and subnets: The VPC and subnets used for the EKS cluster must have routes to the on-premises nodes and pod networks.
    • Cross-Account Elastic Network Interfaces (X-ENIs): Hybrid Nodes use X-ENIs for communication with AWS.
    Note: AWS VPC CNI is not supported on Hybrid Nodes. Use Cilium or Calico instead.

    Firewall Rules

    The following ports must be allowed:

    Table 3. List of ports
    Component Protocol Direction Port Source Destination Purpose
    Cluster Security Group HTTPS Inbound 443 Remote Node CIDRs Kubernetes API Server Kubelet to API Server
    Cluster Security Group HTTPS Outbound 10250 API Server Remote Nodes API Server to Kubelet
    On-Prem Firewall HTTPS Outbound 443 Remote Nodes EKS X-ENI IPs Kubelet to API Server
    On-Prem Host TCP/UDP Inbound/ Outbound 53 Remote Pods CoreDNS DNS Resolution

    In addition to the ports listed above, if using the Dell PowerMax for storage, port 8443 (HTTPS) must be allowed (Inbound/Outbound) in order for the PowerMax CSI driver to access the REST API that is part of Unisphere for PowerMax. Other optional ports used in this solution are: 22 (SSH), 80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS), and 3389 (RDP).

Overview

  • This section outlines the deployment and configuration of AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes with Dell PowerMax as the backing storage.

    Before deploying AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes, the following prerequisites must be met:

    • The PowerMax array is the storage platform used in this solution. Either a PowerMax 2500 or 8500 model can be used. It should be configured and installed with connectivity to the Hybrid Nodes. While this solution calls for Fibre Channel, the PowerMax supports many protocol options that you can use with the PowerMax CSI driver.
    • Ensure that all necessary AWS networking components, including VPC, subnets, and connectivity between AWS and the on-premises data center, are properly configured. This includes opening the proper firewall ports.
      • When using the PowerMax CSI driver, the REST server runs on port 8443. Whether using embedded or external, the Unisphere for PowerMax IPs should be on the same network as the Hybrid Nodes.
    • Create a bastion or jump server in AWS that has connectivity to the on-premises environment. This is used for remote access and administration.
    • Install three bare metal nodes with a supported OS, such as Ubuntu 24.04. These nodes should have the following qualities:
      • Network connectivity to AWS. The IP network should be the same as the one used by Unisphere for PowerMax.
      • Connectivity to the PowerMax array. The PowerMax CSI driver supports FC, iSCSI, NFS, and NVMeoF protocols.

PowerMax

  • The PowerMax family represents the flagship products of the Dell Technologies enterprise storage business. It is designed with a multi-node, active/active scale-out architecture using industry standard, end-to-end NVMe components. The platform features inline, global deduplication and compression, providing customers with high storage efficiency even as the system scales. The PowerMax family also provides what many consider to be the gold standard in data services, proven high availability and resiliency, and advanced security that adheres to stringent government regulations and corporate compliance requirements, such as FIPS 140-2. A core strength of the PowerMax family is its ability to consolidate workloads. One can use a single PowerMax system for Mainframe and Open Systems block storage, and for file storage services as well.

    The PowerMax family of arrays has four models:

    • PowerMax 2500 with a maximum capacity of 8 PBe (Petabytes effective) that can operate in open systems, mainframe, or mixed open systems and mainframe environments
    • PowerMax 2000 with a maximum capacity of 1.2 PBe that can operate in open systems environments
    • PowerMax 8500 with a maximum capacity of 18 PBe that can operate in open systems, mainframe, or mixed open systems and mainframe environments
    • PowerMax 8000 with a maximum capacity of 4.5 PBe that can operate in open systems, mainframe, or mixed open systems and mainframe environments

    PowerMax systems are modular enabling them to expand to meet the future needs of the customer.

PowerMax CSI driver values file parameters

  • Table 6. PowerMax CSI driver values file parameters
    Parameter Description Required Default
    global This section refers to configuration options for both CSI PowerMax Driver and Reverse Proxy. - -
    defaultCredentialsSecret

    This secret name refers to:

    1 The proxy credentials if the driver is installed with proxy.

    2. The default Unisphere credentials if credentialsSecret is not specified for a management server.

    		 Yes powermax-creds
    storageArrays This section refers to the list of arrays managed by the driver and Reverse Proxy. - -
    storageArrayId This refers to PowerMax Symmetrix ID. Yes 000000000001

    backupEndpoint This refers to the URL of the backup Unisphere server managing storageArrayId, if Reverse Proxy is installed. If authorization is enabled, backupEndpoint should be the HTTPS localhost endpoint that the authorization sidecar will listen on. Yes https://backup-1.unisphe.re:8443
    managementServers This section refers to the list of configurations for Unisphere servers managing PowerMax arrays. - -
    endpoint This refers to the URL of the Unisphere server. If authorization is enabled, the endpoint should be the HTTPS localhost endpoint that the authorization sidecar will listen on. Yes https://primary-1.unisphe.re:8443

    skipCertificateValidation This parameter should be set to false if you want to do client-side TLS verification of Unisphere for PowerMax SSL certificates. No “True”
    certSecret The name of the secret in the same namespace containing the CA certificates of the Unisphere server. Yes, if skipCertificateValidation is set to false Empty
    limits This refers to various limits for Reverse Proxy. No -

    maxActiveWrite This refers to the maximum concurrent WRITE request handled by the reverse proxy. No 4

The value that you specify here must be unique. Ensure that no other CSI PowerMax driver is managing the same arrays that are configured with the same prefix. The maximum length for this prefix is three characters. Yes “ABC”

PowerMaxOS operating system

  • PowerMaxOS is the software operating environment for PowerMax arrays. It manages the storage and controls communications with the host systems. There are additional features for PowerMaxOS that provide specific capabilities such as remote replication. The software for PowerMax is available in packages that consist of a core set of features and additional, optional features. For PowerMaxOS 5978 and earlier, there are two packages for open systems arrays and two for mainframe arrays. For PowerMaxOS 10 there is one package, plus an optional SRDF package.

Prepare on-premises credentials provider

  • To enable secure communication between AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes and AWS Systems Manager (SSM), you must create an SSM hybrid activation. This activation allows on-premises nodes to register with AWS Systems Manager, enabling management and monitoring capabilities.

    By default, SSM hybrid activations remain active for 24 hours. You can specify an expiration date longer than that, however you only need the activation to connect the Hybrid Nodes so it should be unnecessary.

    Note: SSM hybrid activation code is displayed only once when created. It must be securely saved as it is needed during node bootstrap. If lost, a new hybrid activation must be generated.

    If the CloudFormation template was used for deployment as detailed in this paper, the IAM role associated with Hybrid Nodes is named the following.

    AmazonEKSHybridNodesRole
    Run the SSM hybrid activation command.

    Running this command on the AWS jump box creates the activation.

    Syntax:

    aws ssm create-activation \
        --default-instance-name <name> \
        --iam-role <role> \
        --registration-limit <limit>

    The parameters are defined as:

    • default-instance-name: Assigns a default name to the activated instances. It can be any name.
    • iam-role: Specifies the IAM role (default is AmazonEKSHybridNodesRole) that grants required permissions.
    • registration-limit: Defines the maximum number of nodes that can register with this activation.

    Supply the parameters and run.

    Command 
    aws ssm create-activation \
        --default-instance-name hybrid-ssm-node \
        --iam-role AmazonEKSHybridNodesRole \
        --registration-limit 4
    Result 
    {
        "ActivationId": "c355490f-2c7f-987b-8068-c364e3fddc7b",
        "ActivationCode": "ESQx1lwstRT6TqOEH9dZ"
    }

    Record the values for use in the next section.

Prerequisites

  • As the AWS EKS cluster cannot be created from the on-premises Hybrid Nodes, you must instantiate a bastion or jump host in AWS. This is a secure server (such as, EC2 instance) in the public subnet that acts as a gateway between the AWS environment and the customer environment. Communication through firewall ports must be enabled as previously covered in the List of ports table. The instance serves as the management node for the EKS cluster. There are several steps you must complete before creating the cluster.

    Note: Although the root user performs the commands in this test environment, in a production configuration sudo is recommended.

    This deployment used an Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 instance. Note that while you can use a Windows instance for the EKS deployment, a Linux instance is required to install the CSI driver as an emulation on Windows (such as, Git Bash) is not supported.

    Perform the following steps on the AWS jump box:

    • Install AWS CLI
    • Configure AWS CLI credentials
    • Configure on-premises IAM credential provider (SSM)
    • Install Helm on the Jump Box

Prerequisites

  • Configure AWS CLI credentials

    1. Update credentials with session token.

      AWS recommends using AWS IAM Identity Center credentials automatically with the  aws configure sso command. Using this method ensures that you do not have to manually update a credentials file regularly . If that is not possible, credentials can be set by using AWS environment variables like so (note the TOKEN is shortened in this example):

      export AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID="ASIA4XX3JSTKEOQO6EY7"
export AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY="A2CddGitXgDTxfJ1AD5/MApPvyNAVR+/26dHR4K/"
export AWS_SESSION_TOKEN="IQoJb3JpZ2luX2VjEGsaCXVzLWVhc3QtMSJHMEUCICXy/tYri/VfZ5mlBG9J/wYYMra3y1Yc+/xY8SoDrmsBAiEA5ntVsKPi1Zklll+="

      Alternatively, manually configure AWS credentials by updating the credentials file located at:

      • Windows:
        C:\Users\<UserName>\.aws\credentials
      • Linux/macOS:
        ~/.aws/credentials

      Add the following details:

      [default]
aws_access_key_id = <YourAccessKeyId>
aws_secret_access_key = <YourSecretAccessKey>
aws_session_token = <YourSessionToken>
    2. Verify configuration.

      Once set, run the following command to confirm the identity associated with the configured credentials.

      Command
      aws sts get-caller-identity
      Result
      {
    "UserId": "URTIROPKJSDHTRHJEWJQTE: first.last@dell.com",
    "Account": "345087217345",
    "Arn": "arn:aws:sts::345087217345:assumed-role/AWSReservedSSO_Acme_tt00g6e30t99c0d2/first.last@dell.com"
}

Prerequisites

  • Configure on-premises IAM credential provider (SSM)

    AWS Systems Manager (SSM) is used for hybrid node authentication. Follow these steps to configure.

    1. Download the CloudFormation template. 
      curl -OL 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aws/eks-hybrid/refs/heads/main/example/hybrid-ssm-cfn.yaml'
    2. Create a cfn-ssm-parameters.json file.

      The file requires a ROLE_NAME, TAG_KEY, and TAG_VALUE. The role name defaults to AmazonEKSHybridNodesRole and the tag key to EKSClusterARN.

      { "Parameters": { "RoleName": "ROLE_NAME", "SSMDeregisterConditionTagKey": "TAG_KEY", "SSMDeregisterConditionTagValue": "TAG_VALUE" }}

      If you accept the defaults, you only supply the TAG_VALUE which is in the format: arn:aws:eks:AWS_REGION:AWS_ACCOUNT_ID:cluster/CLUSTER_NAME.

      In this example both defaults are accepted so only a single parameter is required. Note here that the CLUSTER_NAME is what you name your cluster in a later step.

      { "Parameters": { "SSMDeregisterConditionTagValue": "arn:aws:eks:us-east-1:483945604938:cluster/hybrid-eks" }}
    3. Deploy the CloudFormation stack.
      Command 
      export STACK_NAME=hybrid-ssm
      aws cloudformation deploy \
      --stack-name ${STACK_NAME} \
      --template-file hybrid-ssm-cfn.yaml \
      --parameter-overrides file://cfn-ssm-parameters.json \
      --capabilities CAPABILITY_NAMED_IAM
      Result 
      Waiting for changeset to be created..
      Waiting for stack create/update to complete
      Successfully created/updated stack - hybrid-ssm

  • Install Helm on the Jump Box

    Helm is a package manager for Kubernetes required for managing Kubernetes applications on EKS. Depending on your jump box OS it may be installed already.

    1. Download Helm.
      • Go to the Helm GitHub Releases page.
      • Download the latest Helm version 3 file that matches your OS.
    2. Install Helm.
      • Extract the downloaded file.
      • Add executable privilege and move the helm binary to a directory included in the system’s PATH such as /usr/bin.
    3. Verify Installation.
      Command

Solution architecture

  • The architecture in the following figure represents the two components of the AWS EKS Hybrid Nodes solution. In the AWS Cloud at the top is the EKS cluster control plane which includes the EC2 jump box instance for management, while at the bottom are the EKS Hybrid Nodes running the Kubernetes worker nodes of the cluster. AWS Direct Connect provides a high-bandwidth, low-latency connection from the cloud to the local data center while the AWS Site-to-Site VPN is a private, encrypted connection that is only used in the event AWS Direct Connect is unavailable.

    The Kubernetes API server, located in the AWS Cloud, orchestrates the containerized applications, scheduling them on the local Hybrid Nodes. The Dell PowerMax CSI driver runs on the worker nodes and enables the provisioning of persistent volumes (PVs) to these applications, offering capabilities such as snapshotting and expansion.

Summary

  • The integration of Amazon EKS Hybrid Nodes with Dell PowerMax empowers organizations to adopt a flexible, scalable, and secure hybrid cloud strategy without compromising performance or operational consistency. By leveraging enterprise-grade storage alongside Kubernetes orchestration, businesses can run mission-critical applications seamlessly across environments while meeting stringent data governance and resilience requirements. This solution not only future-proofs infrastructure but also accelerates digital transformation by combining the best of cloud-native technologies with trusted on-premises capabilities.

Unisphere for PowerMax

  • Unisphere for PowerMax is an HTML5 web-based application that enables you to provision, operate and maintain PowerMax, VMAX All Flash, and VMAX storage systems.

    Unisphere for PowerMax 10.2.0.x supports:

    • Storage systems (PowerMax 2500 and PowerMax 8500) running PowerMaxOS 10 (6079)
    • Storage systems (PowerMax 2000, PowerMax 8000, VMAX 250F, VMAX 450F, VMAX 850F, and VMAX 950F) running PowerMaxOS 5978
    • Storage systems (VMAX 100K, VMAX 200K, VMAX 400K, VMAX 250F, VMAX 450F, VMAX 850F, and VMAX 950F) running HYPERMAX OS 5977

    A Representational State Transfer (REST) API is also built into Unisphere for PowerMax. The REST API allows you to access diagnostic, performance, and configuration data, as well as perform provisioning operations on the storage system through interfaces like the CSI driver. Full documentation for the Unisphere for PowerMax REST API is available at developer.dell.com or from the Help menu within the Unisphere for PowerMax User Interface.
